newsitem.title: USA: Naomi Campbell says October Versace show will go on.
newsitem.headline: Naomi Campbell says October Versace show will go on.

text.p: International supermodel Naomi Campbell, who was reportedly very close to slain fashion designer Gianni Versace, on Wednesday said she would take part in a planned October showing of Versace's creations in Milan.

"We have to still go on to keep his name, and the most important thing is that we know that he would want us to be doing his show here in Milan in October, so that's what I'm going to do," she told ABC's "Good Morning America."
Pausing at times to hold back tears, Campbell also said: "And it probably will be my only show that I do."

Campbell was interviewed from Milan, where on Tuesday she and scores of the top names in fashion and entertainment attended a memorial service for the 50-year-old designer, who was shot and killed last week outside his mansion in Miami.

No one has been arrested in connection with the murder. The prime suspect is Andrew Cunanan, described by police as a gay prostitute, who is also wanted in connection with the murder of four other men in a nationwide killing spree.
Campbell said she and other friends and fans of Versace's hope "that they find this person that's out there that's done this horrible, tragic crime."
She said Versace's legacy would be that he was "well-respected and loved because he was so generous and so caring and sympathetic to other people's problems ... he's just a very special person."
